Open `GWAS_course.Rproj` and work from the project root. Run the chunks in order in a fresh R session.
All data are simulated. Read each summary, run its chunk and compare your result with the expected result.
The linked step pages explain the ideas and provide troubleshooting.

You need the full [checkpoint at step 2.8](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-2/step-2-8) before you start.

```{r module3_check}
if (!file.exists("config.R") && file.exists("../config.R")) setwd("..")
source("R/guided.R"); guided_check_module(3)
```

```{r module3_setup}
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
```

## Step 3.1 · Rough cleaning

We remove samples and variants with very many missing calls. This first clean prevents the worst failures from distorting the checks that follow.

[Read step 3.1 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-1).

```{r s3-1}
# 1. Choose the input files and the names for the saved files.
input <- guided_path(cfg, "2.8")
rough <- guided_path(cfg, "3.1", "samples")
# 2. Remove samples with more than 10% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", input, "--mind", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", rough))
# 3. Remove variants with more than 10% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", rough, "--geno", "0.10", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.1")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.1", "2.8")
guided_register(cfg, "3.1", "2.8", 2013, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

**Command 1: remove poor samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--mind` | Removes samples with more than 10% missing calls. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove poor variants**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--geno` | Removes variants with more than 10% missing calls in the input dataset. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

Three wells and 150 variants are removed. 2,013 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --mind 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_samples --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_samples --geno 0.10 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-1_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

## Step 3.2 · Sample call rate

We remove samples with more than 2% of their genotype calls missing. This keeps samples with enough information for the later analysis.

[Read step 3.2 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-2).

```{r s3-2}
# 1. Remove samples with more than 2% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.2")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.2", "3.1")
guided_register(cfg, "3.2", "3.1", 1971, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--mind` | Removes samples with more than 2% missing calls, keeping a call rate of at least 98%. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

42 more wells are removed. 1,971 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

## Step 3.3 · Recorded and genetic sex

We compare recorded sex with patterns in the X and Y chromosome calls. We remove flagged wells from this teaching analysis because a mismatch needs review before the sample is used.

[Read step 3.3 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-3).

```{r s3-3}
# 1. Choose names for the chromosome files and sex report.
split <- guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "par")
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "sexcheck")
# 2. Label the regions shared by the X and Y chromosomes.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.2"), "--split-par", "b38", "--make-pgen", "--out", split))
# 3. Compare recorded sex with the X and Y chromosome results.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", split, "--check-sex", "max-female-xf=0.2", "min-male-xf=0.8",
  "max-female-ycount=100", "min-male-ycount=1000", "--out", report))
# 4. Read the report and list samples that need to be removed.
sexcheck <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".sexcheck"))
bad <- sexcheck$IID[sexcheck$STATUS != "OK"]
remove_file <- guided_list(bad, guided_path(cfg, "3.3", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
# 5. Save the dataset without the flagged samples.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", split, "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.3")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.3", "3.2", extra = data.frame(option = "--split-par", value = "b38"))
guided_register(cfg, "3.3", "3.2", 1963, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

**Command 1: label the shared X and Y regions**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--split-par` | Uses GRCh38 boundaries (b38) to label the shared regions of X and Y separately. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: compare recorded sex with DNA**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--check-sex` | Compares recorded sex with X chromosome patterns and the number of observed Y calls. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `max-female-xf` | Sets 0.2 as the largest X coefficient accepted for a recorded female. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `min-male-xf` | Sets 0.8 as the smallest X coefficient accepted for a recorded male. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `max-female-ycount` | Accepts at most 100 observed Y calls for a recorded female. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `min-male-ycount` | Requires at least 1000 observed Y calls for a recorded male. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 3: remove samples flagged by the sex check**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

Eight flagged wells are removed. 1,963 samples remain. 520 sites are labelled PAR1 or PAR2. The number of variants does not change.

## Step 3.4 · LD pruning

We pick a set of common variants that are not strongly linked to each other. The sample checks that follow need independent variants, otherwise the same genetic signal is counted many times.

[Read step 3.4 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-4).

```{r s3-4}
# 1. Write the list of regions where nearby variants are strongly linked.
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)
# 2. Select variants with less similar patterns of DNA letters.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--chr", "1-22", "--maf", "0.05", "--geno", "0.02",
  "--exclude", "bed1", regions, "--indep-pairwise", "200kb", "0.2", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune")))
# 3. Check and print how many variants were selected.
pruned <- readLines(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"))
stopifnot(length(pruned) == 69539L)
cat(length(pruned), "variants kept by LD pruning\n")
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "3.4", c(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), c(".prune.in", ".prune.out")), regions), parent = "3.3")
```

### What each option does

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--chr` | Uses only chromosomes 1 to 22, the autosomes. |
| `--maf` | Keeps variants whose less common allele has a frequency of at least 5%. |
| `--geno` | Keeps variants with no more than 2% missing calls. |
| `--exclude` | Leaves out variants within the listed DNA regions. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `bed1` | Reads DNA regions with positions counted from 1 and includes both ends of each region. |
| `--indep-pairwise` | Selects a less strongly linked set within windows of 200 kb (200,000 DNA bases), using a squared correlation limit of 0.2. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

The `.prune.in` file lists 69,539 sites. The complete analysis state still has 296,360 variants.

### PLINK terminal equivalent

These commands are shown for reference. Run the R chunk above to follow the course.
R creates any lists needed between PLINK commands. On Windows, use `bin\plink2.exe`.

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed1 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed1 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2 --out results/guided/s3-4_prune --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

## Step 3.5 · Heterozygosity

We check whether each sample has unusually many or few genotypes with two different alleles. We remove the unusually high-heterozygosity samples and keep the low-heterozygosity samples flagged for review, because an unusual value alone does not prove an error.

[Read step 3.5 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-5).

```{r s3-5}
# 1. Choose the name for the report of matching DNA letters.
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "het")
# 2. Measure matching DNA letters using the selected variants.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--extract", paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"), "--het", "--out", report))
# 3. Read the report and calculate the average and spread of F.
het <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".het"))
f <- as.numeric(het$F)
mean_f <- mean(f); sd_f <- sqrt(mean((f - mean_f)^2))
# 4. Find samples with unusually low or high F values.
low <- het$IID[f < mean_f - 3 * sd_f]
high <- het$IID[f > mean_f + 3 * sd_f]
# 5. Save the high F review list and the low F removal list.
guided_list(high, guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "flag_high.txt"), TRUE)
remove_file <- guided_list(low, guided_path(cfg, "3.5", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
# 6. Save the dataset without the low F samples.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.5")))
# 7. Print the average, spread and numbers of flagged samples.
print(c(mean_F = mean_f, SD_F = sd_f, low_removed = length(low), high_flagged = length(high)))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.5", "3.3")
guided_register(cfg, "3.5", "3.4", 1950, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

**Command 1: measure matching DNA letters**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--extract` | Uses only the variants named in the supplied variant list. |
| `--het` | Reports how often each sample has two matching alleles, compared with what the allele frequencies predict. R uses this report to calculate F and the review thresholds. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove samples with unusually few matching letters**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

13 wells with low F are removed. Eight wells with high F are flagged and kept. The mean F is approximately 0.0078. The population SD is approximately 0.0298. 1,950 samples remain.

```sh

bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --remove results/guided/s3-5_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-5_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

## Step 3.6 · Relatedness and duplicates

We compare pairs of samples to find repeated measurements and close relatives. We apply the stated removal rules so that repeated or closely related people do not distort the later association analysis.

[Read step 3.6 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-6).

```{r s3-6}
# 1. Choose the name for the report comparing pairs of samples.
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "king")
# 2. Compare pairs using the selected variants.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.5"), "--extract", paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"),
  "--make-king-table", "--king-table-filter", "0.0442", "--out", report))
# 3. Read the pairs and put the closest matches first.
kin <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".kin0"))
kin <- kin[order(-as.numeric(kin$KINSHIP)), ]
# 4. Read the sample details and start an empty removal list.
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
remove <- character()
# 5. Review each pair to decide which samples to remove.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(kin))) {
  a <- kin$IID1[i]; b <- kin$IID2[i]; value <- as.numeric(kin$KINSHIP[i])
  # 6. Treat the closest matches as repeated samples.
  if (value > 0.354) {
    # 7. Remove the labelled repeat when its name ends in _R2.
    if (endsWith(a, "_R2") || endsWith(b, "_R2")) {
      remove <- union(remove, if (endsWith(a, "_R2")) a else b)
    } else {
      # 8. Compare sex, age and disease status for unlabelled repeats.
      ai <- match(a, metadata$IID); bi <- match(b, metadata$IID)
      same <- identical(unname(unlist(metadata[ai, c("SEX", "Age", "Disease")])),
                        unname(unlist(metadata[bi, c("SEX", "Age", "Disease")])))
      # 9. Keep one matching record or remove both conflicting records.
      remove <- union(remove, if (same) max(a, b) else c(a, b))
    }
  # 10. Keep one person from each remaining closely related pair.
  } else if (value > 0.177 && !a %in% remove && !b %in% remove) remove <- union(remove, max(a, b))
}
# 11. Write the removal list.
remove_file <- guided_list(remove, guided_path(cfg, "3.6", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
# 12. Save the dataset without the listed samples.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.5"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.6")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.6", "3.5")
guided_register(cfg, "3.6", "3.5", 1920, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

**Command 1: compare pairs of samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--extract` | Uses only the variants named in the supplied variant list. |
| `--make-king-table` | Estimates how closely related each pair of samples is and writes a table. |
| `--king-table-filter` | Writes only pairs with estimated kinship above 0.0442, an approximate screening boundary for third-degree relatives such as first cousins. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove repeated or closely related samples**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

There are 19 duplicate-class pairs and ten first-degree pairs. In total, 30 records are removed. 1,920 samples remain. Pairs can overlap, because one person can be in more than one pair. For this reason, the pair counts are not counts of unique people.

## Step 3.7 · Batch effects

We compare the fraction of successful genotype calls across laboratory plates. We remove the faulty plate in these simulated data because samples processed together can share technical problems.

[Read step 3.7 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-7).

```{r s3-7}
# 1. Choose the name for the missing-call report.
report <- guided_path(cfg, "3.7", "missing")
# 2. Count missing calls for each sample.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.6"), "--missing", "sample-only", "--out", report))
# 3. Read the report and match each sample to its laboratory plate.
missing <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".smiss"))
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
plate <- metadata$Plate[match(missing$IID, metadata$IID)]
# 4. Calculate and print the middle call rate for each plate.
median_missing <- tapply(as.numeric(missing$F_MISS), plate, median)
print(sort(1 - median_missing))
# 5. Find the plate with the most missing calls and check its name.
worst <- names(which.max(median_missing))
stopifnot(worst == "P14")
# 6. Write the list of samples from the faulty plate.
remove_file <- guided_list(missing$IID[plate == worst], guided_path(cfg, "3.7", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
# 7. Save the dataset without samples from that plate.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.6"), "--remove", remove_file, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.7")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.7", "3.6")
guided_register(cfg, "3.7", "3.6", 1844, 296360, operations = ops)
```

### What each option does

**Command 1: measure missing calls by sample**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--missing` | Writes a report of missing genotype calls. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&rarr; `sample-only` | Writes one row per sample and skips the report for variants. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

**Command 2: remove samples from the faulty plate**

| Option or modifier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--pfile` | Reads the PGEN, PVAR and PSAM input files that share the given name prefix. |
| `--remove` | Removes the samples named in the supplied sample list. |
| `--make-pgen` | Saves a new dataset as PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files. |
| `--out` | Sets the shared beginning of the output file names. |

Every command also uses `--threads 2` (PLINK runs at most two tasks at the same time) and `--memory 2048` (PLINK uses at most about 2 GB of memory).

### Expected result

Plate P14 has a median call rate of approximately 98.56%. The other plates have 99.84%. The 76 remaining wells of plate P14 are removed. 1,844 samples and 296,360 variants remain.

```sh

bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-6_state --remove results/guided/s3-7_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-7_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

## Step 3.8 · Sample QC summary and checkpoint

We save the complete dataset after sample quality control and review the recorded counts. This gives us a checked starting point for variant quality control in module 4.

[Read step 3.8 on the course website](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/module-3/step-3-8).

```{r s3-8}
# 1. Save a complete copy of the dataset after sample checks.
guided_snapshot(cfg, "3.8", guided_path(cfg, "3.7"), 1844, 296360, parent = "3.7")
# 2. Print the recorded sample and variant counts.
print(read.delim(file.path(cfg$out, "step_counts.tsv")))
# 3. Check that the saved files have the expected counts.
check_step("3.8", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

### What each option does

No PLINK options are used in this step.

### Expected result

Module 3 boundary: 1,844 samples and 296,360 variants. The restart operations for the steps in between are stored. The complete main-path package supplies full genotype copies at steps 2.8, 3.8, 4.6 and 5.7. Steps 4.6 and 5.7 are the ends of later modules. You can rebuild the states in between from the previous full checkpoint and the stored replay operations.

### PLINK terminal equivalent

No PLINK equivalent
